assumptions_made: Used the synthetic_text_to_sql dataset as a proxy for 2D point clouds, extracting numerical features
When the dataset didn't provide suitable numeric features, fell back to synthetic data generation
Generated synthetic data with three Gaussian blobs at different separation levels (0.5, 1.0, 2.0) to represent increasing overlap
Used Adjusted Rand Index as the primary metric to compare k-means against random assignment
Used the same number of clusters (3) for both k-means and random assignment
Applied StandardScaler to normalize features before clustering
Used KMeans from scikit-learn with default parameters except for fixed random seed

results.hypothesis: Test whether k-means recovers known cluster structure better than random assignment at increasing overlap.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: Random assignment of points to the same number of clusters.
results.success_criteria: k-means beats random assignment on adjusted Rand index at every separation level tested.
results.notes: Separation 0.5: k-means ARI=0.483, random ARI=-0.004, better; Separation 1.0: k-means ARI=0.960, random ARI=-0.012, better; Separation 2.0: k-means ARI=1.000, random ARI=-0.002, better
results.methodological_validity: synthetic surrogate data — the pipeline is exercised but the findings are NOT interpretable as evidence for or against the hypothesis
